title: Resume an SDDC LCM fleet component upgrade across an access token expiry
prompt:
Implement `src/com/broadcom/vcf/sddclcm/SddcLcmClient.java` as a JDK-only VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC LCM client. Edit no other file and add no dependency; the only helper you may call is the supplied `com.broadcom.vcf.sddclcm.Json` codec.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/sddc-lcm/sddc-lcm-openapi.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba`. Its provenance is repeated in `docs/official_sources.json`, including the spec path, the commit sha and a pinned source record for every operationId. No rendered documentation page is a contract source. Use exactly the specification operationIds `getHealth`, `getComponents`, `resolveDepotComponents`, `performComponentAction` and `getTask`; call no other route. The pinned document declares the `bearerToken` scheme but no token issuance or refresh operation, so session renewal goes through the supplied `AccessTokenSource` and never over the wire.

Preserve the supplied public API and types: `create(String serviceRootUrl, AccessTokenSource tokens, HttpClient httpClient)`, `upgradeFleetComponent(UpgradeRequest)`, `AccessTokenSource`, `UpgradeRequest`, `UpgradeOutcome`, `SddcLcmException`, `ApiException`, `ProtocolException` and `TaskFailureException`. A null `HttpClient` means `HttpClient.newHttpClient()`. Reject with `IllegalArgumentException` a blank, schemeless or non-HTTP(S) service root, a service root carrying a query or fragment, a null token source, a null request, a blank `componentType`, `targetVersion`, `fleetDepotFqdn` or `fleetDepotCertificate`, a `correlationId` that is not a bare uuid, and a held access token that is blank or unsafe to place in a header. Every one of those rejections must happen before any request reaches the service. Never put either access token into an exception message or into a result.

`upgradeFleetComponent` runs one fleet component upgrade in this order. First `getHealth`: a bodyless request with no `Authorization` header at all, because that operation carries an operation-level empty security list; require HTTP 200 and `up` true. Then `getComponents` with `scope=FLEET` as its only query member; require HTTP 200 and exactly one listed component whose `componentType` matches the request, and keep that component's `id` and `version`. A listed entry whose `scope` is not `FLEET`, no match, or more than one match is a `ProtocolException` naming `getComponents`. Then `resolveDepotComponents` with a `DepotComponentsSpec` carrying `fleetDepotSpec` (its `fqdn` then its `certificate`) followed by `componentVersions` holding the single `{component, version}` entry; the optional top-level `version` is unset and omitted. Require HTTP 200 and the `binaryUrl` the depot resolved for that component and target version.

Then `performComponentAction` with `action=precheck` on the component id. Its `ComponentUpgradeSpec` body carries `componentSpec` only, and that `componentSpec` carries `software` (with `version`) then `depot` (with `url`). `lcmPlatformSpec`, `correlationId`, `policy`, `userInput`, `additionalInput` and `DepotSpec.certificate` are all unset and omitted, and the optional `X-Correlation-Id` header is not sent. Require HTTP 202 and keep the returned task id. Poll `getTask` on that id until it reports a terminal `TaskStatus` of `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED` or `CANCELED`, then stop polling. Anything other than `SUCCEEDED` raises `TaskFailureException` and the apply is never submitted.

Then `performComponentAction` with `action=apply` on the same component. Its body carries `componentSpec` (with `software.version`, then `depot.url`, then `depot.certificate` as a one-element array holding the fleet depot certificate), then `lcmPlatformSpec` (with `performBackup`), then `correlationId`; send the same correlation value in the declared `X-Correlation-Id` header. Require HTTP 202, then poll the apply task the same way and report the outcome.

The access token the session starts with stops being accepted once the precheck task finishes, so the apply submission is answered HTTP 401. On the first 401 of the run only, call `AccessTokenSource.refreshAccessToken()` exactly once, adopt the replacement token and resend the identical interrupted request: same target, same body bytes, same `X-Correlation-Id`, with only the `Authorization` value changed. Do not replay the health probe, the component listing, the depot resolution or the precheck submission, do not renew for any other status, and do not renew a second time when the resumed request is refused again. Report the renewal count as `UpgradeOutcome.accessTokenRefreshes`.

Honor the exact wire contract. Every authenticated request carries exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <current access token>` and exactly one `Accept: application/json`. Every bodyless request omits `Content-Type` and sends no body. Every request with a body sends exactly one `Content-Type: application/json` and the compact `Json.write` encoding of an insertion-ordered map, so members appear in the declaration order `docs/contract.json` records. An operation that declares no query parameter carries no `?` at all; `getComponents` carries exactly `?scope=FLEET` and `performComponentAction` exactly `?action=precheck` or `?action=apply`. Omitting an unset optional member means it is absent from the wire: never null, never an empty string, never an empty array or object, never a false default, and never a bare delimiter.

Run `bash run-verification.sh`. It compiles the client together with the protected harness and runs twelve scenarios. Each one starts the shipped contract-pinned fixture on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port and reads its synchronized request log; the fixture loads its only callable routes, their authentication requirement and their declared parameters from `docs/contract.json`. Verification asserts the exact ten-request expiry, renewal and resume sequence, raw request targets, header multiplicity, encoded body bytes, token rotation, the identical resend of the interrupted apply, the absence of replayed work, the single-renewal policy, and the omission of every unset optional member. The verifier never contacts a live VMware endpoint.
scenario: A fleet component precheck succeeds, the session access token stops being accepted, the apply submission returns HTTP 401, the caller-supplied token source mints one replacement, and the identical apply submission resumes without replaying the listing, the depot resolution or the precheck.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves exact optional-member omission, unauthenticated health probing, single-renewal token rotation, and resume without replayed work.
